candidates.video_title: The Fruit in Your Kitchen Is Radioactive 🍌
candidates.video_description: Bananas contain a naturally occurring radioactive element called Potassium-40. Scientists even use bananas as a unit of radiation measurement. Would you still eat one? 🍌☢️ #funfacts #didyouknow #science #bananas #radiation #mindblowing #shorts
candidates.script: The fruit sitting in your kitchen right now is technically radioactive. Bananas contain a naturally occurring radioactive element called Potassium-40. Scientists actually created a unit of measurement called the Banana Equivalent Dose — meaning they measure radiation levels by comparing them to bananas. Eating one banana exposes you to about 0.1 microsieverts of radiation. To put that in perspective, you would need to eat around 10 million bananas at once to receive a lethal dose. So your morning smoothie is completely safe — but here is the real question: how many bananas have you eaten in your lifetime?

candidates.topic: Cleopatra closer to iPhone than pyramids
candidates.teaser: Kleopatra, piramitlerden çok daha yakın bir zamanda yaşadı — ve bu seni şaşırtacak.
candidates.video_title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the iPhone Than Pyramids
candidates.video_description: The pyramids of Giza were built around 2560 BC, while Cleopatra lived around 69 BC — that's a gap of roughly 2,500 years. The iPhone was released in 2007, making Cleopatra closer to us in time than to the pyramid builders. History is stranger than you think. 🏛️📱 #history #cleopatra #pyramids #mindblowing #didyouknow #facts #shorts
candidates.script: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the invention of the iPhone than to the construction of the Great Pyramids. Think about that for a second. The pyramids were built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born in 69 BC — that is a gap of nearly 2,500 years between her and the pyramid builders. But from Cleopatra to today? Only about 2,090 years. The iPhone launched in 2007, which means she is literally closer to your pocket device than to one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. So the next time someone calls history boring — what other facts like this have been hiding in plain sight?

candidates.video_title: This Animal Has 3 Hearts — And It Gets Weirder 🐙
candidates.video_description: Octopuses have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, while one pumps it to the rest of the body. Shockingly, two of those hearts stop beating when an octopus swims. That's why they prefer crawling. Nature is wild. 🐙💙 #octopus #animals #oceanlife #didyouknow #funfacts #mindblowing #shorts
candidates.script: Octopuses have not one, not two, but three hearts — and what happens to two of them will completely change how you see these creatures. Two hearts work exclusively to pump blood through the gills, while the third pumps it to the rest of the body. But here is where it gets wild: when an octopus swims, two of those three hearts actually stop beating entirely. That is why octopuses prefer crawling along the ocean floor — swimming literally exhausts their cardiovascular system. Oh, and their blood is blue because it contains copper instead of iron. So if you could have any animal's biology, would you really pick three hearts that fail when you move?

candidates.teaser: Uzayda bir patlama olsa bile sen onu asla duyamazsın — ve sebebi düşündüğünden farklı.
candidates.video_title: Why Explosions in Space Are Completely Silent 🚀
candidates.video_description: Sound needs a medium like air or water to travel through — and space is a near-perfect vacuum. Even a supernova explosion, one of the most violent events in the universe, produces zero sound for any listener in space. The universe has been exploding in total silence for billions of years. 🌌 #space #universe #science #didyouknow #funfacts #nasa #shorts
candidates.script: If a star exploded right next to your spaceship, you would hear absolutely nothing. Sound is not a wave that travels on its own — it needs molecules to pass through, like air or water. Space is a near-perfect vacuum, meaning there are almost no molecules at all. A supernova, which is one of the most catastrophic explosions in the entire universe, releases more energy in seconds than our sun will produce in its entire lifetime — and it does all of that in complete, total silence. Every star that has ever died, every galaxy collision, every cosmic event in history — all of it happened without a single sound. Does that make the universe feel more beautiful or more terrifying to you?

candidates.teaser: İnsan vücudu gerçekten ışık yayıyor — ama gözlerimiz bunu görmek için çok zayıf.
candidates.video_title: Your Body Actually Glows in the Dark 🌟
candidates.video_description: The human body emits a very faint visible light through a process called biophoton emission. This glow is about 1,000 times weaker than what the human eye can detect, but Japanese scientists captured it on camera in 2009. You are literally a glowing being. ✨ #humanbody #science #biology #didyouknow #mindblowing #funfacts #shorts
candidates.script: Your body is glowing right now, and you have absolutely no idea. Humans emit a faint visible light called biophotons — produced by chemical reactions happening inside your cells every single second. In 2009, Japanese scientists used an ultra-sensitive camera in a pitch-dark room and actually photographed the human glow. The light is about 1,000 times too dim for our eyes to detect on their own. Interestingly, the glow is not constant — it is strongest in the late afternoon and weakest just before sunrise, almost like your body has its own internal light cycle. So the real question is: if you could see this glow with your naked eye, what do you think you would look like?
